clue.text: Look inside: great ape

parts.note: the punctuation mark printed in the clue is itself called a colon
OS is the abbreviation for outsize, i.e. great in size
to ape is to imitate or copy

explanation.surface: A command to peer inside, followed by a description of a huge gorilla.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon looks like mere punctuation separating definition from wordplay, but it supplies the first five letters by its name.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical procedure is an internal examination of the bowel with a camera, literally a look inside.

clue.text: May has been one time I can be away (rest, I'm in plays)

indicators.note: away suggests the letters are sent astray, out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: plays suggests the letters move about freely into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Theresa May once served; now she can step aside and rest in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' rearranges T I CAN BE; 'plays' rearranges REST I'M IN. Theresa May was Home Secretary when this was set.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa May, then Home Secretary, had served in the cabinet, being one of its senior members.

clue.text: GP team starts to treat unlikely symptoms by the book, briefly

indicators.note: briefly says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a log is a record book, like a ship's logbook

indicators.note: starts to points to the first letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: A GP's medical team begin treating odd symptoms strictly according to the manual.
explanation.walkthrough: GP looks like a family doctor but means Grand Prix; Lotus was a Formula One team.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotus is a racing car maker that ran a team in Grand Prix motor racing.

clue.text: Compound tax for dummies?

parts.note: a nit is a fool or dummy
a rate is a local tax

explanation.surface: Is there a compound tax rate explained simply for beginners?
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's order is 'tax for dummies', but the answer reads as a rate for nits.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt of nitric acid is a chemical compound.

clue.text: Fledgling business in sheep, the main attraction!

parts.note: the star is the headline act, the main attraction
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A new farming firm whose top draw is its flock.
explanation.definitionFit: A newly founded company is a fledgling business, just learning to fly.

clue.text: On mobile, manages abroad

indicators.note: on mobile means heard over the phone, so the sound of the word counts

parts.note: to oversee is to supervise or manage

explanation.surface: Someone runs things by mobile phone while away from home.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseas means in a foreign country, abroad.

clue.text: New Labour's Lie (my original film)

indicators.note: original suggests a novel, inventive rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A political documentary exposing a Blair-era falsehood, presented as one's own work.
explanation.walkthrough: New Labour was Tony Blair's rebranded Labour Party of the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of the 1968 Beatles animated film.

clue.text: Where Sicilians are provided with one motive

definitions.meaning: having a single unifying motif, as a party built around one idea

explanation.definitionFit: Split as two words it is the sea around Sicily; whole, it describes something organised around a unifying subject.

clue.text: Support in boxing ring for army

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Backing for a fighter in the boxing ring, from the forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman legion was a large army unit, and the word now means any great host or army.

clue.text: Home truth — a bit attracted to host

indicators.note: the words truth, a bit and attracted host the answer, holding it within their run of letters

explanation.surface: A frank admission that someone was a little drawn to the idea of entertaining guests.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature's natural environment is where it lives, its home.

clue.text: Inflamed areas aloe vera treated, very lacking

indicators.note: treated suggests the remaining letters are processed into a new arrangement
lacking says the letter for very is missing from the plant name

explanation.surface: Sore patches of skin were soothed with aloe vera, though not much of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' drops V from ALOE VERA, leaving ALOEERA, which 'treated' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Areolae are small rings of reddish skin, such as the inflamed zone surrounding a pimple or pustule.

clue.text: Screw's foot has twisted way towards face

parts.note: Screw is the setter, so the setter's thing is 'mine'

indicators.note: twisted says the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A screw's pointed end has been bent on its way into a wall's surface.
explanation.walkthrough: Screw is the setter's pseudonym; setters often refer to themselves to give ME or MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertical pit shaft is the passage miners take down to the coal face.

clue.text: One sumo wrestling in Finland, as locals would say

indicators.note: wrestling suggests the letters grappling into a new order

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A single sumo bout taking place in Finland, described in the local tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Finnish-language name for the country of Finland.

clue.text: Info's slightly retrospective

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a tad means slightly or a little

explanation.surface: A claim that some information is a bit backward-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Info and data are both synonyms for facts and figures collected for use.

clue.text: Follow beat, spoken in different pattern

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are set out in a different pattern, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: Musical advice: follow the beat, but speak your words in another rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor someone closely is to follow what they are doing, an idiom.

clue.text: Rolling performance after mine

indicators.note: after says the fuss comes after the mine word

parts.note: an oil well is a source mined for oil, a kind of mine
a to-do is a fuss, a performance

explanation.surface: A barrel rolling around after a show down the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling' is the definition in its sense of 'rolling in it', very rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling, as in rolling in money, is a slang way of saying wealthy or affluent.

clue.text: Every other air raid with drop is dazzling

indicators.note: every other letter of the two words is taken, starting from the second

parts.note: a descent is a drop or fall

explanation.surface: Every second aerial bombing raid, with bombs dropping, makes a brilliant display.
explanation.definitionFit: Shimmering with rainbow colours that change with the light, which is dazzling to look at.

clue.text: Native to steal from raised local houses

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the pub holds the theft

parts.note: a local is a British term for one's nearby pub or inn

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is turned upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: to rob is to steal

explanation.surface: A local resident pinches things from the pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Native and inborn both mean innate, present from birth.

clue.text: Reported those hacking into bank

indicators.note: reported means as said aloud, so the sound gives the word

parts.note: people with a hacking cough are coughers

explanation.surface: Computer hackers were reported to have broken into a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacking' suggests computer hackers but means coughing.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffers are strongboxes holding money, the funds of an institution, like a bank's reserves.

clue.text: More on edge, close to canyon — mistake to film struggle

indicators.note: close to points to the final letter of the word after it
to film is to cover with a film, so one word coats the other

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
to vie is to struggle or compete

explanation.surface: A more anxious crew near the canyon's edge, with an error in shooting a fight scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervier is the comparative of nervy, which means jittery or on edge.

clue.text: Honest chap ultimately skewered Kipper's situation

parts.note: Abraham Lincoln was nicknamed Honest Abe

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A trustworthy man has finally skewered a smoked herring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kipper' looks like the smoked fish but here means someone kipping; 'kip' is British slang for sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taking a kip, or sleep, is in bed.

clue.text: How long mother's been alive to harm

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
how long one has been alive is one's age

explanation.surface: A question about how old someone's mother is, ending in harm.
explanation.definitionFit: To damage something is to harm or injure it.

clue.text: Belting main inhabitant

definitions.meaning: belting is British slang for excellent, like 'brilliant' shortened
the main is the sea, and this flatfish related to the turbot lives there

explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal shorthand for brilliant, and also names a European flatfish of the sea.

clue.text: In France, the slicing weapon's reason for 999 call?

indicators.note: slicing says the French word cuts into the weapon

parts.note: a firearm is a gun, a weapon
la is French for the (feminine)

explanation.surface: A French blade is the reason someone dialled the emergency number.
explanation.walkthrough: 999 is the British emergency telephone number.
explanation.definitionFit: A building's ringing warning bell is a cause to phone the emergency services, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Counters one clique's cut with recession

indicators.note: with recession means going back, so the shortened word is turned around
cut says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a cabal is a clique
one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: An economic recession has cut the finances of a group of insiders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recession' looks like economics, but here it means going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: These are frames of beads on wires used for counting, so they are counters.

clue.text: Her supply, with a lot in seedy place

indicators.note: supply read as supple-ly, i.e. bendily, so the letters are flexed into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman's stock, with plenty of it, kept in a run-down spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A squalid, dirty dwelling or den is a seedy place, likened to where rodents live.

clue.text: Picturing Prince Harry's admission, without the Queen

indicators.note: without says the royal letters are removed

parts.note: Prince Harry has red hair, so he might confess 'I'm a ginger'
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A royal confession, minus his grandmother, about what he looks like.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a red-haired person is called a ginger; 'without' removes ER from IMAGINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Creating pictures, as with medical scans, is picturing.

clue.text: Space that may be let for dining option

parts.note: room means space
in tennis a serve can be called a let and replayed, so a service may be let

explanation.surface: An area for rent that offers a choice of meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space that may be let' reads like a room for rent; in tennis a let is a serve that clips the net and is replayed.
explanation.definitionFit: In a hotel, having meals brought to your quarters is one dining option.
